132	def move_plugin_directory_to_trash(path: Path, label: str = "") -> Path:
133	    """Atomically rename a plugin directory into the trash area.
134	
135	    Either the whole directory moves or nothing changes: when a file inside is
136	    locked (e.g. a plugin DLL loaded by a running IDA on Windows), the rename
137	    fails without modifying the installation.
138	
139	    The optional label is included in the trashed name (e.g. ".rollback") so
140	    a human inspecting the trash can tell what a leftover was.
141	
142	    Raises:
143	        PluginInUseError: when the rename fails because files are in use.
144	    """
145	    trash_dir = get_trash_directory(path.parent)
146	    trash_dir.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
147	    destination = trash_dir / f"{path.name}{label}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
148	    try:
149	        os.rename(path, destination)
150	    except OSError as e:
151	        if is_file_in_use_error(e):
152	            raise PluginInUseError(path.name, path) from e
153	        raise
154	    return destination

157	def remove_plugin_directory(path: Path) -> None:
158	    """Remove a plugin directory transactionally.
159	
160	    First atomically rename the directory into the trash area, then delete the
161	    trashed copy. If deletion fails, the plugin is already logically removed;
162	    the leftover is swept by a later plugin command.
163	
164	    Raises:
165	        PluginInUseError: when files are in use; the installation is untouched.
166	    """
167	    trashed = move_plugin_directory_to_trash(path)
168	    try:

170	    except OSError as e:
171	        logger.debug("could not delete trashed directory %s: %s (leaving for later sweep)", trashed, e)

174	def sweep_trash() -> None:
175	    """Best-effort cleanup of leftovers in the trash area.
176	
177	    Leftovers accumulate from interrupted operations: partially deleted
178	    uninstalls, staging directories, stale upgrade rollbacks. Call this only
179	    between plugin operations, never while one is in flight: an active upgrade
180	    keeps its rollback copy in the trash.
181	    """
182	    try:
183	        trash_dir = get_trash_directory()
184	        if not trash_dir.is_dir():
185	            return
186	        entries = list(trash_dir.iterdir())
187	    except Exception as e:
188	        logger.debug("could not enumerate trash directory: %s", e)
189	        return
190	
191	    for entry in entries:
192	        logger.debug("sweeping trash: %s", entry)
193	        try:
194	            if entry.is_dir() and not entry.is_symlink():
195	                shutil.rmtree(entry)
196	            else:
197	                entry.unlink()
198	        except OSError as e:
199	            logger.debug("could not sweep %s: %s", entry, e)

534

536	        PipNotAvailableError: If pip is not available in IDA's Python
537	        DependencyInstallationError: If dependencies cannot be installed, including when
538	            IDA's Python environment fails the health check (see `validate_python_environment`).
539	    """
540	    python_dependencies = get_python_dependencies_from_plugin_archive(zip_data, metadata)
541	    if python_dependencies:

543	        for existing_plugin_path in get_installed_plugin_paths():

571	def validate_can_install_plugin(
572	    zip_data: bytes,
573	    metadata: IDAMetadataDescriptor,
574	    current_platform: str,
575	    current_version: str,
576	    pip_options: PipOptions = PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT,
577	    check_environment: bool = True,
578	) -> Path | None:
579	    """Verify plugin can be installed.
580	
581	    Returns:
582	        The Python executable path if pip dependencies were validated, None otherwise.
583	
584	    Raises:
585	        InvalidPluginNameError: If plugin name is invalid
586	        PluginAlreadyInstalledError: If plugin is already installed
587	        BrokenPluginInstallationError: If remnants of a broken installation are in the way
588	        PlatformIncompatibleError: If current platform is not supported
589	        IDAVersionIncompatibleError: If current IDA version is not supported
590	        PipNotAvailableError: If pip is not available (when dependencies are needed)
591	        DependencyInstallationError: If dependencies cannot be installed
592	    """
593	    name = metadata.plugin.name
594	    try:
595	        destination_path = get_plugin_directory(name)
596	    except ValueError as e:
597	        logger.error(f"Can't install plugin: {e!s}")
598	        raise InvalidPluginNameError(name, str(e)) from e
599	
600	    # is_symlink() is checked in addition to exists() so a broken symlink
601	    # (dangling editable install) is reported rather than tripping up
602	    # extraction later.
603	    if destination_path.exists() or destination_path.is_symlink():
604	        if is_valid_plugin_directory(destination_path):
605	            logger.warning(f"Plugin directory already exists: {destination_path}")
606	            raise PluginAlreadyInstalledError(name, destination_path)
607	
608	        # The directory exists but doesn't hold a working plugin: remnants of
609	        # an interrupted install/uninstall (issue #228). Point the user at
610	        # uninstall, which knows how to remove broken directories, rather than
611	        # silently deleting data on the install path.
612	        logger.warning(f"Broken plugin directory: {destination_path}")
613	        raise BrokenPluginInstallationError(name, destination_path)
614	
615	    platforms = metadata.plugin.platforms
616	    if current_platform not in platforms:
617	        logger.warning(f"Current platform not supported: {current_platform}")
618	        raise PlatformIncompatibleError(current_platform, platforms)
619	
620	    if metadata.plugin.ida_versions and not is_ida_version_compatible(current_version, metadata.plugin.ida_versions):
621	        logger.warning(f"Current IDA version not supported: {current_version}")
622	        raise IDAVersionIncompatibleError(current_version, metadata.plugin.ida_versions)
623	
624	    return validate_can_install_python_dependencies(
625	        zip_data, metadata, pip_options=pip_options, check_environment=check_environment
626	    )

629	def validate_archive_entry(file_info: zipfile.ZipInfo, relative_path: pathlib.PurePosixPath) -> None:
630	    """Validate a ZIP archive entry before extraction.
631	
632	    This function prevents path traversal attacks by rejecting:
633	    - Symlinks (which can point outside the extraction directory)
634	    - Absolute paths
635	    - Paths containing '..' (parent directory references)
636	
637	    Raises:
638	        ValueError: If the entry is unsafe to extract
639	    """
640	    # Reject symlinks - they can escape the extraction directory
641	    # Unix symlink has file type 0xA in the high nibble of external_attr
642	    if (file_info.external_attr >> 28) == 0xA:
643	        logger.warning("Rejecting symlink in archive: %s", file_info.filename)
644	        raise ValueError(f"Symlinks not allowed in archive: {file_info.filename}")
645	
646	    # Reject absolute paths
647	    if relative_path.is_absolute():
648	        logger.warning("Rejecting absolute path in archive: %s", file_info.filename)
649	        raise ValueError(f"Absolute path in archive: {file_info.filename}")
650	
651	    # Reject path traversal sequences
652	    if ".." in relative_path.parts:
653	        logger.warning("Rejecting path traversal in archive: %s", file_info.filename)
654	        raise ValueError(f"Path traversal in archive: {file_info.filename}")
655	
656	
657	def should_extract_plugin_archive_path(plugin_dir_prefix: str, file_info: zipfile.ZipInfo) -> bool:
658	    """Should the given file entry be extracted for the given plugin directory in a zip archive?
659	
660	    Args:
661	      plugin_dir_prefix: the path within the ZIP archive to the plugin to extract
662	      file_info: the entry to consider
663	    """
664	    if not file_info.filename.startswith(plugin_dir_prefix):
665	        # only consider entries within the plugin directory
666	        return False
667	
668	    if file_info.filename == plugin_dir_prefix:
669	        # don't extract the plugin directory entry itself
670	        return False
671	
672	    if file_info.filename.startswith(plugin_dir_prefix + ".git/"):
673	        # don't extract git repo junk, which comes from manually archiving a plugin source repo
674	        return False
675	
676	    relative_path = pathlib.PurePosixPath(file_info.filename).relative_to(plugin_dir_prefix.rstrip("/"))
677	    # don't extract the plugin directory entry itself (again)
678	    return str(relative_path) != "."

681	def extract_zip_subdirectory_to(zip_data: bytes, subdirectory: Path, destination: Path):
682	    """Extract a subdirectory from a zip archive to a destination path."""
683	    if destination.exists():
684	        raise FileExistsError(f"Destination already exists: {destination}")
685	
686	    with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(zip_data)) as zip_file:
687	        if not subdirectory or subdirectory == Path("."):
688	            # subdirectory represents the root (e.g., None or Path("."))
689	            plugin_dir_prefix = ""
690	        else:
691	            plugin_dir_prefix = subdirectory.as_posix() + "/"
692	
693	        # Stage in the trash area beside the destination's plugins directory
694	        # rather than in the system temp dir: (normally) the same filesystem,
695	        # so the final rename is atomic on all platforms and the fully-formed
696	        # plugin directory appears all at once. An interrupted install never
697	        # leaves a partial destination, and abandoned staging directories are
698	        # swept by later plugin commands.
699	        staging_root = get_trash_directory(destination.parent)
700	        staging_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
701	        temp_path = staging_root / f"{destination.name}.staging-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
702	        temp_path.mkdir()
703	
704	        try:
705	            # do validation pass before extracting any content to prevent any half-extracted content
706	            for file_info in zip_file.infolist():
707	                if not should_extract_plugin_archive_path(plugin_dir_prefix, file_info):
708	                    continue
709	
710	                relative_path = pathlib.PurePosixPath(file_info.filename).relative_to(plugin_dir_prefix.rstrip("/"))
711	                validate_archive_entry(file_info, relative_path)
712	
713	            for file_info in zip_file.infolist():
714	                if not should_extract_plugin_archive_path(plugin_dir_prefix, file_info):
715	                    continue
716	
717	                relative_path = pathlib.PurePosixPath(file_info.filename).relative_to(plugin_dir_prefix.rstrip("/"))
718	                target_path = temp_path / relative_path
719	
720	                if file_info.is_dir():
721	                    logger.debug("creating directory: %s", relative_path)
722	                    target_path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
723	                else:
724	                    target_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
725	                    try:
726	                        with zip_file.open(file_info.filename) as source_file, target_path.open("wb") as target_file:
727	                            logger.debug("creating file:      %s", relative_path)
728	                            shutil.copyfileobj(source_file, target_file)
729	                    except OSError as e:
730	                        if e.errno == errno.ENOSPC:
731	                            raise NoSpaceError(target_path.parent) from e
732	                        raise
733	
734	            logger.debug("creating plugin directory: %s", destination)
735	            os.rename(temp_path, destination)
736	        except BaseException:
737	            shutil.rmtree(temp_path, ignore_errors=True)
738	            raise

816	def pack_plugin_directory_to_zip(source_dir: Path) -> bytes:
817	    """Pack a plugin source directory into an in-memory ZIP archive, files
818	    placed at the archive root. The resulting bytes can be fed straight into
819	    `install_plugin_archive`, so a local directory install reuses the same
820	    validation and extraction logic as a remote/zip install.
821	
822	    Skips common dev junk so an in-place git checkout doesn't poison the
823	    install with `.git/`, `__pycache__/`, etc.
824	    """
825	    buf = io.BytesIO()
826	    with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, mode="w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zf:

837	def install_plugin_directory_editable(
838	    source_dir: Path, name: str, pip_options: PipOptions = PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT, check_environment: bool = True
839	):
840	    """Install a plugin from a local source directory by symlinking it into
841	    $IDAUSR/plugins/<name>.
842	
843	    Edits to files in `source_dir` take effect on the next plugin reload, with
844	    no re-install needed -- the standard development workflow for plugin
845	    authors.
846	
847	    Python dependencies declared in `ida-plugin.json` are installed the same
848	    way as a regular install. The destination path is replaced if it already
849	    exists (file, directory, or stale symlink), but the source directory is
850	    never touched.
851	    """
852	    source_dir = source_dir.resolve()
853	    metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_directory(source_dir)
854	    validate_metadata_in_plugin_directory(source_dir)
855	
856	    if metadata.plugin.name != name:
857	        raise ValueError(
858	            f"plugin name mismatch: caller passed '{name}', ida-plugin.json declares '{metadata.plugin.name}'"
859	        )
860	
861	    logger.info("installing plugin (editable): %s (%s)", metadata.plugin.name, metadata.plugin.version)
862	
863	    with rich.status.Status("finding IDA installation", console=stderr_console):
864	        current_platform = find_current_ida_platform()
865	        current_version = find_current_ida_version()
866	
867	    platforms = metadata.plugin.platforms
868	    if current_platform not in platforms:
869	        logger.warning(f"Current platform not supported: {current_platform}")
870	        raise PlatformIncompatibleError(current_platform, platforms)
871	
872	    if metadata.plugin.ida_versions and not is_ida_version_compatible(current_version, metadata.plugin.ida_versions):
873	        logger.warning(f"Current IDA version not supported: {current_version}")
874	        raise IDAVersionIncompatibleError(current_version, metadata.plugin.ida_versions)
875	
876	    try:
877	        destination_path = get_plugin_directory(metadata.plugin.name)
878	    except ValueError as e:
879	        logger.error(f"Can't install plugin: {e!s}")
880	        raise InvalidPluginNameError(metadata.plugin.name, str(e)) from e
881	
882	    # Validate + install Python dependencies. Excludes the current plugin from
883	    # the existing-installed set so a re-install of the same plugin doesn't
884	    # double-count its own deps when verifying the resolver.
885	    python_dependencies = get_python_dependencies_from_plugin_directory(source_dir, metadata)
886	    if python_dependencies:
887	        with rich.status.Status("collecting existing Python dependencies", console=stderr_console):
888	            all_python_dependencies: list[str] = []
889	            for existing_plugin_path in get_installed_plugin_paths():
890	                try:
891	                    existing_metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_directory(existing_plugin_path)
892	                except Exception as e:
893	                    logger.debug("skipping unreadable plugin metadata at %s: %s", existing_plugin_path, e)
894	                    continue
895	                if existing_metadata.plugin.name == metadata.plugin.name:
896	                    continue
897	                existing_deps = get_python_dependencies_from_plugin_directory(existing_plugin_path, existing_metadata)
898	                all_python_dependencies.extend(existing_deps)
899	            all_python_dependencies.extend(python_dependencies)
900	
901	        python_exe = resolve_python_for_dependencies(python_dependencies, check_environment=check_environment)
902	
903	        try:
904	            verify_pip_can_install_packages(python_exe, all_python_dependencies, pip_options=pip_options)
905	        except CantInstallPackagesError as e:
906	            raise DependencyInstallationError(python_dependencies, str(e)) from e
907	
908	        with rich.status.Status(
909	            f"installing Python dependencies: {', '.join(python_dependencies)}", console=stderr_console
910	        ):
911	            try:
912	                pip_install_packages(python_exe, all_python_dependencies, pip_options=pip_options)
913	            except CantInstallPackagesError:
914	                logger.debug("can't install dependencies")
915	                raise
916	
917	    # Remove any existing install at the target. is_symlink() is checked
918	    # before exists() because a broken symlink fails exists() but should
919	    # still be replaced.
920	    if destination_path.is_symlink() or destination_path.is_file():
921	        destination_path.unlink()
922	    elif destination_path.exists():
923	        remove_plugin_directory(destination_path)
924	
925	    try:
926	        destination_path.symlink_to(source_dir, target_is_directory=True)
927	    except OSError as e:
928	        raise ValueError(
929	            f"Failed to create symlink {destination_path} -> {source_dir}: {e}. "
930	            "On Windows, symlink creation requires Developer Mode or "
931	            "administrator privileges."
932	        ) from e
933	
934	    logger.info("symlinked %s -> %s", destination_path, source_dir)
935	
936	    # If the project uses the standard src-layout, drop a .pth file into IDA's
937	    # site-packages so the package is importable. This mirrors what
938	    # `pip install -e .` does (PEP 660). For flat-layout projects, IDA already
939	    # exposes the plugin directory on sys.path (because plugin.py is exec'd
940	    # from there), so no .pth is needed -- but we still clear any stale one
941	    # left over from a prior src-layout install.
942	    src_dir = source_dir / "src"

945	    else:
946	        _remove_editable_pth_file(metadata.plugin.name)

955	    """Return IDA's Python site-packages directory (purelib).

958	    ``--target``. Uses sysconfig on the IDA-side interpreter so the result

991	def _uninstall_broken_plugin_directory(name: str) -> None:
992	    """Remove a plugins/<name> entry that is not a valid installation.
993	
994	    Remnants of an interrupted uninstall (e.g. rmtree failed partway because a
995	    running IDA held a DLL open, issue #228) don't count as installed, but the
996	    entry blocks reinstallation. The user asked for this name to be gone, so
997	    remove whatever is squatting on it: a broken directory, a stale symlink,
998	    or even a plain file.
999	
1000	    Raises:
1001	        PluginNotInstalledError: If no matching entry exists at all
1002	        PluginInUseError: If files are in use; nothing is modified
1003	    """
1004	    plugins_dir = get_plugins_directory()
1005	    for child in plugins_dir.iterdir():
1006	        if child.name.lower() != name.lower():
1007	            continue
1008	
1009	        logger.warning("removing remnants of a broken plugin installation: %s", child)
1010	        if child.is_symlink():
1011	            child.unlink()
1012	            _remove_editable_pth_file(child.name)
1013	        elif child.is_file():
1014	            child.unlink()
1015	        else:
1016	            remove_plugin_directory(child)
1017	        return
1018	
1019	    raise PluginNotInstalledError(name)

1022	def uninstall_plugin(name: str):
1023	    """Remove an installed plugin.
1024	
1025	    Transactional: the plugin directory is first atomically renamed into the
1026	    trash area, then deleted. When plugin files are locked (e.g. loaded by a
1027	    running IDA on Windows), the rename fails without modifying anything.
1028	
1029	    Raises:
1030	        PluginNotInstalledError: If plugin is not installed
1031	        PluginInUseError: If plugin files are in use; the installation is untouched
1032	    """
1033	    try:
1034	        record = find_installed_plugin(name)
1035	    except PluginNotInstalledError:
1036	        # a directory may exist without being a valid installation (issue #228)
1037	        _uninstall_broken_plugin_directory(name)
1038	        return
1039	
1040	    logger.info("uninstalling plugin: %s (%s)", record.name, record.version)
1041	
1042	    # note that the pythonDependencies of the plugin aren't pruned.
1043	    # we could re-collect all the deps requested by other plugins
1044	    # but we shouldn't do a sync, since there might be other utils installed by the user.
1045	    # so I think its better to just leave the orphans around.
1046	
1047	    if record.path.is_symlink():
1048	        # Editable install (or a manually-symlinked plugin): remove the
1049	        # symlink only. Calling shutil.rmtree on a directory symlink raises
1050	        # on POSIX and recurses into the target on some Windows configs --
1051	        # both wrong; we want to leave the source tree untouched.
1052	        record.path.unlink()
1053	        # Editable installs may have dropped a .pth into IDA's site-packages
1054	        # to expose a src-layout package. Best-effort cleanup.
1055	        _remove_editable_pth_file(record.name)
1056	    else:
1057	        remove_plugin_directory(record.path)

1111	def upgrade_plugin_archive(
1112	    zip_data: bytes, name: str, pip_options: PipOptions = PIP_OPTIONS_DEFAULT, check_environment: bool = True
1113	):
1114	    path, metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_archive(zip_data, name)
1115	    validate_metadata_in_plugin_archive(zip_data, path, metadata)
1116	
1117	    if not is_plugin_installed(metadata.plugin.name):
1118	        raise PluginNotInstalledError(metadata.plugin.name)
1119	
1120	    current_platform = find_current_ida_platform()
1121	    current_version = find_current_ida_version()
1122	
1123	    validate_can_upgrade_plugin(
1124	        zip_data,
1125	        metadata,
1126	        current_platform,
1127	        current_version,
1128	        pip_options=pip_options,
1129	        check_environment=check_environment,
1130	    )
1131	
1132	    plugin_path = get_plugin_directory(metadata.plugin.name)
1133	    existing_metadata = get_metadata_from_plugin_directory(plugin_path)
1134	
1135	    new_version = parse_plugin_version(metadata.plugin.version)
1136	    existing_version = parse_plugin_version(existing_metadata.plugin.version)
1137	
1138	    if new_version <= existing_version:
1139	        logger.warning(
1140	            f"New version {metadata.plugin.version} is not greater than existing version {existing_metadata.plugin.version}"
1141	        )
1142	        raise PluginVersionDowngradeError(
1143	            metadata.plugin.name, existing_metadata.plugin.version, metadata.plugin.version
1144	        )
1145	
1146	    # Checkpoint: atomically move the current install into the trash area
1147	    # before writing anything. When plugin files are locked (e.g. loaded by a
1148	    # running IDA on Windows), this fails without modifying the installation.
1149	    # The unique trash name means a stale rollback from an interrupted upgrade
1150	    # never blocks this one; the sweep removes such leftovers later.
1151	    rollback_path = move_plugin_directory_to_trash(plugin_path, label=".rollback")
1152	
1153	    try:
1154	        install_plugin_archive(zip_data, name, pip_options=pip_options, check_environment=check_environment)
1155	    except Exception as e:
1156	        # note that Python dependencies installed before the failure aren't
1157	        # rolled back; they're upgraded in place and left as-is.
1158	        logger.debug("error during upgrade: install: %s", e)
1159	        logger.debug("rolling back to prior version")
1160	        shutil.rmtree(plugin_path, ignore_errors=True)
1161	        if plugin_path.exists():
1162	            logger.error(
1163	                "could not restore previous version: partial upgrade remains at %s; uninstall and reinstall",
1164	                plugin_path,
1165	            )
1166	        else:
1167	            os.rename(rollback_path, plugin_path)
1168	        raise
1169	    else:
1170	        try:
1171	            shutil.rmtree(rollback_path)
1172	        except OSError as e:
1173	            logger.debug("could not delete rollback copy %s: %s (leaving for later sweep)", rollback_path, e)

1	"""Parsing and normalization helpers for plugin references.
2	
3	A plugin reference is a user-supplied string that names a plugin and may
4	optionally qualify it with a version spec and/or a repository URL (host).
5	
6	Accepted forms:
7	    name
8	    name==1.2.3
9	    name@https://github.com/org/repo
10	    name==1.2.3@https://github.com/org/repo
11	    repo/name
12	    repo/name==1.2.3@https://github.com/org/repo
13	
14	The module is intentionally free of Click/Rich so it can be unit tested easily.
15	"""
16	
17	from __future__ import annotations
18	
19	import re
20	from dataclasses import dataclass
21	from urllib.parse import urlparse
22	
23	from hcli.lib.ida import PLUGIN_REPOSITORY_NAME_CHARS
24	from hcli.lib.ida.plugin import GITHUB_REPOSITORY_PATTERN, PORTAL_REPOSITORY_PATTERN
25	
26	# The shapes that may identify a plugin, taken from the schema module that
27	# validates them: one definition, so a reference hcli parses and an identity
28	# hcli accepts can never drift apart. Compiled case-insensitively here because
29	# a user typing a reference is not held to the casing a descriptor declares.
30	_GITHUB_REPO_RE = re.compile(GITHUB_REPOSITORY_PATTERN, re.IGNORECASE)
31	_PORTAL_REPO_RE = re.compile(PORTAL_REPOSITORY_PATTERN, re.IGNORECASE)
32	
33	# broader match that also accepts ``.git`` suffix and ``@tag`` for direct
34	# installs (e.g. ``https://github.com/org/repo.git@v1.0``).
35	_GITHUB_DIRECT_INSTALL_RE = re.compile(
36	    r"^https://github\.com/[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+/[a-zA-Z0-9._-]+"
37	    r"(?:\.git)?(?:@[a-zA-Z0-9._/+-]+)?/?$",
38	    re.IGNORECASE,
39	)
40	
41	
42	# A leading "repo/" scopes the lookup. The character class comes from the
43	# config module that validates repository names, so a name hcli accepts is
44	# always a prefix hcli can parse. Plugin names are ``^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+$``, so a
45	# "/" can only ever be this separator.
46	_REPO_PREFIX_RE = re.compile(rf"^([{PLUGIN_REPOSITORY_NAME_CHARS}]+)/(.+)$")
47	
48	
49	@dataclass(frozen=True)
50	class PluginReference:
51	    """A parsed plugin reference.
52	
53	    Attributes:
54	        name: bare plugin name.
55	        version_spec: version specifier with operator (``"==1.2.3"``), or ``""`` when absent.
56	        host: normalized code repository URL, or ``None`` when unqualified.
57	        repo: configured plugin repository name to search, or ``None`` for the default.
58	            Lookup scope only: it is dropped once the plugin is resolved and is
59	            never stored, because where a plugin was found is not part of what
60	            it is.
61	    """
62	
63	    name: str
64	    version_spec: str
65	    host: str | None
66	    repo: str | None = None
67	
68	
69	def is_github_repository_url(value: str) -> bool:
70	    """Return True if ``value`` is a whole-string GitHub repository URL.
71	
72	    This differs from ``repo/github.py:is_github_url`` which only checks
73	    whether ``github.com/`` appears somewhere in the string. A qualified
74	    plugin reference like ``foo@https://github.com/org/repo`` must parse as
75	    a reference, not a raw URL, so we use a strict whole-string match here.
76	    """
77	    return bool(_GITHUB_REPO_RE.match(value))
78	
79	
80	def is_plugin_host_url(value: str) -> bool:
81	    """Return True if ``value`` can appear after ``@`` in a plugin reference.
82	
83	    Accepts every shape that can identify a plugin: a GitHub repository, or a
84	    Hex-Rays portal page. Note this is deliberately wider than
85	    ``is_github_direct_install_url``, which stays GitHub-only because it guards
86	    "this string is a raw URL, not a reference".
87	    """
88	    return bool(_GITHUB_REPO_RE.match(value) or _PORTAL_REPO_RE.match(value))
89	
90	
91	def is_github_direct_install_url(value: str) -> bool:
92	    """Return True if ``value`` is a GitHub URL suitable for direct installation.
93	
94	    Accepts the same shapes as ``is_github_repository_url`` plus ``.git``
95	    suffix and ``@tag`` for tagged releases::
96	
97	        https://github.com/org/repo
98	        https://github.com/org/repo.git
99	        https://github.com/org/repo@v1.0
100	        https://github.com/org/repo.git@v1.0
101	
102	    Does NOT match qualified plugin references (``name@https://...``)
103	    because those don't start with ``https://``.
104	    """
105	    return bool(_GITHUB_DIRECT_INSTALL_RE.match(value))
106	
107	
108	def normalize_plugin_host(host: str) -> str:
109	    """Normalize a plugin repository URL for comparison.
110	
111	    The normalization:
112	    - lowercases scheme, netloc, and path;
113	    - strips exactly one trailing slash from the path.
114	
115	    Args:
116	        host: repository URL string, for example ``https://GitHub.com/Org/Repo/``.
117	
118	    Returns:
119	        normalized URL string, for example ``https://github.com/org/repo``.
120	
121	    Raises:
122	        ValueError: when ``host`` cannot be parsed as an absolute URL with scheme and netloc.
123	    """
124	    parsed = urlparse(host)
125	    if not parsed.scheme or not parsed.netloc:
126	        raise ValueError(f"invalid plugin host URL: {host!r}")
127	
128	    scheme = parsed.scheme.lower()
129	    netloc = parsed.netloc.lower()
130	    path = parsed.path.lower()
131	    path = path.removesuffix("/")
132	
133	    return f"{scheme}://{netloc}{path}"
134	
135	
136	def _split_name_and_version(value: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
137	    """Split ``name[op version]`` into ``(name, version_spec)``.
138	
139	    Returns ``(value, "")`` when there's no version spec. The version spec is
140	    returned including the operator (``"==1.2.3"``) so callers can round-trip
141	    the original syntax.
142	
143	    Raises:
144	        ValueError: when the operator looks malformed (e.g. trailing ``=``
145	            without another character).
146	    """
147	    # look for the first operator char
148	    match = re.search(r"[=><!~]", value)
149	    if not match:
150	        return value, ""
151	
152	    op_start = match.start()
153	    name = value[:op_start]
154	    op_chars = value[op_start : op_start + 2]
155	    if len(op_chars) < 2 or op_chars[1] != "=":
156	        raise ValueError(f"invalid plugin version spec: {value!r}")
157	
158	    # operator + remaining characters (the version string)
159	    version_spec = value[op_start:]
160	    return name, version_spec
161	
162	
163	def parse_plugin_reference(value: str) -> PluginReference:
164	    """Parse a plugin reference string.
165	
166	    Supported forms:
167	        name
168	        name==1.2.3
169	        name@https://github.com/org/repo
170	        name==1.2.3@https://github.com/org/repo
171	
172	    The version operator, when present, appears before the ``@repo`` suffix.
173	    The repository suffix is detected by splitting on the last ``@`` and
174	    checking whether the suffix is a whole-string GitHub repository URL.
175	    A string that is itself a raw GitHub repository URL is NOT treated as a
176	    plugin reference and raises ``ValueError``.
177	
178	    Returns:
179	        a ``PluginReference`` with ``host`` normalized when present.
180	
181	    Raises:
182	        ValueError: when the string cannot be parsed (empty name, malformed
183	            operator, etc.).
184	    """
185	    if not value:
186	        raise ValueError("plugin reference is empty")
187	
188	    if is_github_direct_install_url(value):
189	        raise ValueError(f"value is a GitHub URL, not a plugin reference: {value!r}")
190	
191	    # Peel the repository prefix first. No URL can be mistaken for one: the
192	    # pattern requires every character before the first "/" to be [a-z0-9-],
193	    # which "https://..." (colon) and "name@https://..." (at-sign, colon) both
194	    # fail, so a scheme can never parse as a repository name.
195	    repo: str | None = None
196	    prefix_match = _REPO_PREFIX_RE.match(value)
197	    if prefix_match:
198	        repo, value = prefix_match.group(1), prefix_match.group(2)
199	
200	    host: str | None = None
201	    remaining = value
202	    if "@" in value:
203	        left, _, right = value.rpartition("@")
204	        if not is_plugin_host_url(right):
205	            raise ValueError(
206	                f"plugin reference has an '@' but the suffix is not a valid plugin repository URL: {value!r}"
207	            )
208	        host = normalize_plugin_host(right)
209	        remaining = left
210	
211	    if "@" in remaining:
212	        raise ValueError(f"plugin reference name/version must not contain '@': {value!r}")
213	
214	    name, version_spec = _split_name_and_version(remaining)
215	    if not name:
216	        raise ValueError(f"plugin reference has empty name: {value!r}")
217	
218	    if "/" in name:
219	        raise ValueError(f"plugin reference name must not contain '/': {name!r}")
220	
221	    return PluginReference(name=name, version_spec=version_spec, host=host, repo=repo)

224	def format_qualified_plugin_reference(ref: PluginReference) -> str:
225	    """Render a plugin reference in its canonical user-facing string form.
226	
227	    Formats:
228	        name@host
229	        name==1.2.3@host
230	        repo/name==1.2.3@host
231	    """
232	    prefix = f"{ref.repo}/" if ref.repo else ""
233	
234	    if not ref.host:
235	        return f"{prefix}{ref.name}{ref.version_spec}"
236	
237	    return f"{prefix}{ref.name}{ref.version_spec}@{ref.host}"

Now I have a thorough understanding of the entire system. Let me synthesize everything into concrete proposals.

---

Here's what I've gathered and analyzed. Let me lay out the landscape and then present proposals.

## Current State

The `ida-plugin.json` schema (v1) has no inter-plugin dependency mechanism. Each plugin is a self-contained unit installed to `$IDAUSR/plugins/<name>/`. The only dependency concept today is `pythonDependencies` (pip packages). There's already a TODO at `install.py:770`: `# TODO: install idaPluginDependencies`. Multi-plugin archives exist (multiple `ida-plugin.json` files in subdirectories of a single zip), but they're just a packaging convenience for the indexer, not a grouping mechanism for users.

There's no install-reason tracking. When a plugin is uninstalled, its Python deps are left as orphans (by design per comment at `install.py:1044`). The `InstalledPluginRecord` tracks `path`, `metadata`, `name`, `version`, `host` but nothing about *why* or *how* the plugin was installed.

## Two distinct requirements

**Requirement A (high priority):** Tightly-coupled plugin groups that move as a unit. Hex-Rays paid extensions distributed as a collection. Users install/upgrade/uninstall the collection, never individual members. Members shouldn't even appear as individual plugins to the user. This is a product packaging need.

**Requirement B (lower priority):** Loose curated collections ("packs") that are a shortcut to installing several related plugins. After installation, the individual plugins retain their identity and can be managed independently. This is a discoverability/convenience need.

These two requirements have different semantics, but the research overwhelmingly shows that using a single mechanism with different behavioral flags is better than creating two separate systems. Let me show how.

---

## Proposal 1: Unified `dependencies` field with `bundled` flag

This is the apt/Home Assistant hybrid adapted for IDA's constraints. One mechanism, behavioral distinction via a single boolean.

### Schema changes to `ida-plugin.json`

```json
{
  "IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion": 1,
  "plugin": {
    "name": "hexrays-advanced-analysis",
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "init.py",
    "description": "Hex-Rays Advanced Analysis Suite",
    "urls": { "repository": "https://plugins.hex-rays.com/hexrays/advanced-analysis/suite" },
    "authors": [{"name": "Hex-Rays", "email": "support@hex-rays.com"}],
    "idaVersions": ["9.3"],
    
    "dependencies": [
      { "name": "hexrays-taint-engine", "bundled": true },
      { "name": "hexrays-type-propagation", "bundled": true },
      { "name": "hexrays-call-graph-viz", "bundled": true }
    ]
  }
}
```

For a loose pack:
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "go-analysis-pack",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "noop.py",
    "dependencies": [
      { "name": "go-runtime-detector" },
      { "name": "go-string-extractor" },
      { "name": "go-type-recovery" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### `bundled` semantics

When `bundled: true`:
- Members are co-packaged in the same archive as the parent plugin (multi-plugin zip already supported by the format).
- Members are hidden from `hcli plugin status` output; only the parent shows.
- Members cannot be individually installed, upgraded, or uninstalled.
- The parent plugin's version governs the entire set. Upgrade parent = upgrade all members atomically.
- Members install to `$IDAUSR/plugins/<parent-name>/<member-name>/` (subdirectory isolation).

When `bundled` is absent or `false`:
- Members are independent plugins fetched from the repository during install.
- They show individually in `hcli plugin status`.
- After installation, they can be individually upgraded or uninstalled.
- Install-reason tracking records that they were pulled in by the parent.

### Install-reason tracking

New file `$IDAUSR/plugins/.install-state.json`:
```json
{
  "go-string-extractor": {
    "install_reason": "dependency",
    "installed_by": ["go-analysis-pack"],
    "installed_at": "2026-09-16T..."
  },
  "go-analysis-pack": {
    "install_reason": "user",
    "installed_by": [],
    "installed_at": "2026-09-16T..."
  }
}
```

### Command behavior

| Action | Bundled | Non-bundled |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `install parent` | Extract all members from archive into `<parent>/` subdir | Fetch + install each dep from repo, record install reason |
| `uninstall parent` | Remove parent dir (including all members) | Remove parent, mark deps as orphaned. `autoremove` cleans later |
| `upgrade parent` | Atomic: new archive replaces entire subtree | Upgrade parent only; deps upgrade independently |
| `status` | Show parent only, with member count | Show parent + all deps individually |
| `uninstall member` | Refused ("managed by parent") | Allowed, with warning if parent depends on it |

### Pros
- Single mechanism for both use cases, distinguished by one boolean.
- Bundled plugins in a subdirectory keep the plugins dir tidy.
- Bundled deps can be co-packaged in the same archive, so no repository dependency resolution needed for Requirement A.
- No version constraints between plugins needed (bundled travel together; loose deps use whatever version the repo has).

### Cons
- Subdirectory nesting (`plugins/<parent>/<child>/`) requires IDA's plugin loader to recursively scan, or requires the parent's entry point to register child plugins. This is a real constraint that needs IDA-side changes or a workaround.
- `bundled: true` means the dependency resolution is completely static (archive contains everything). Limits flexibility but is correct for the Hex-Rays paid extension use case.
- A pack plugin still needs a no-op entry point file (`noop.py`), which is a bit clunky.

---

## Proposal 2: Two top-level keys: `components` and `dependencies`

This explicitly separates the two concepts at the schema level, like VS Code's `extensionDependencies` vs `extensionPack`, but with important differences to avoid VS Code's known bugs.

### Schema

Tight group (Requirement A):
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "hexrays-advanced-analysis",
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "init.py",
    
    "components": [
      "hexrays-taint-engine",
      "hexrays-type-propagation",
      "hexrays-call-graph-viz"
    ]
  }
}
```

Loose pack (Requirement B):
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "go-analysis-pack",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "noop.py",
    
    "dependencies": [
      "go-runtime-detector",
      "go-string-extractor",
      "go-type-recovery"
    ]
  }
}
```

### `components` semantics
- Must be co-packaged in the same archive.
- Installed/upgraded/removed atomically with the parent.
- Hidden from user-facing listings.
- Install path: `$IDAUSR/plugins/<parent>/<component>/` or a flat layout where the parent's entry point is the orchestrator.
- The component names are *internal* identifiers; users never type them.

### `dependencies` semantics
- Fetched from repository on install.
- Install-reason tracking (same `.install-state.json` as Proposal 1).
- After installation, individually manageable.
- `autoremove` command for orphan cleanup.

### Pros
- Very explicit. No ambiguity about which behavior applies.
- `components` makes the tight-coupling clear: these are not independent plugins.
- Simple arrays of names, no version constraints needed.

### Cons
- Two fields, two code paths, two sets of tests. The VS Code lesson is that this split generates a class of bugs around "is this member a component or a dependency?"
- If you ever want a plugin that has both tight components AND loose dependencies, the interaction between the two fields needs careful definition.
- `components` is a new concept that doesn't correspond to anything in the existing plugin manager. `dependencies` at least has the precedent of `pythonDependencies`.

---

## Proposal 3: `pluginType` field with role-based semantics

Instead of annotating dependencies, annotate the *plugin itself* with its structural role. The role determines how it behaves in the plugin manager.

### Schema

Parent plugin manifest for a tight group:
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "hexrays-advanced-analysis",
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "init.py",
    "pluginType": "suite"
  }
}
```

Member plugin manifests (co-packaged in the same archive):
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "hexrays-taint-engine",
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "taint.py",
    "pluginType": "component",
    "memberOf": "hexrays-advanced-analysis"
  }
}
```

Loose pack:
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "go-analysis-pack",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "noop.py",
    "pluginType": "pack",
    "dependencies": [
      "go-runtime-detector",
      "go-string-extractor"
    ]
  }
}
```

### `pluginType` values
- `"plugin"` (default): normal standalone plugin, current behavior.
- `"suite"`: a plugin that serves as the anchor for co-packaged components. Multi-plugin archive; members declare `memberOf` pointing back.
- `"component"`: a plugin that belongs to a suite. Cannot be independently installed/upgraded/removed. Must declare `memberOf`.
- `"pack"`: a plugin whose main purpose is to pull in `dependencies`. Its entry point may be a no-op or a thin orchestrator.

### Multi-plugin archive behavior for suites

The existing multi-plugin archive support already handles multiple `ida-plugin.json` files in a single zip. Today, installing from such an archive requires specifying which plugin to install. For suites, `hcli plugin install hexrays-advanced-analysis` would:
1. Find the suite plugin in the archive.
2. Discover all plugins with `memberOf: "hexrays-advanced-analysis"` in the same archive.
3. Install the suite + all components together.

### Pros
- Self-describing: each plugin knows its own role.
- The `memberOf` back-reference enables discovery within multi-plugin archives naturally.
- Clean separation between "this plugin IS a component of something" vs "this plugin DEPENDS on something."
- Composable: a suite member could itself have `dependencies` on loose plugins.

### Cons
- Introduces three new values for `pluginType`, which is more surface area.
- The `memberOf` field creates a bidirectional relationship (parent lists nothing; children point to parent), which is the opposite direction of Proposals 1 and 2 (parent lists children). This means the parent manifest doesn't declare its members, which makes it harder to validate completeness of a suite archive.
- A bit of a kitchen-sink design; each combination of `pluginType` + other fields has different behavior.

---

## Proposal 4: Minimal `dependencies`-only with install-mode flags at the command level

Don't encode the tight/loose distinction in the manifest at all. Instead, put it at the command level and in the install-state tracking.

### Schema

Same manifest for both cases, just a `dependencies` array:
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "hexrays-advanced-analysis",
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "init.py",
    "dependencies": [
      "hexrays-taint-engine",
      "hexrays-type-propagation"
    ]
  }
}
```

### Command-level distinction

For tight groups, the co-packaging happens at the archive level (multi-plugin zip, already supported) and the install command has a `--managed` flag or recognizes that all deps are present in the same archive:

```
hcli plugin install hexrays-advanced-analysis
```

When HCLI detects that all declared dependencies are co-packaged in the same archive, it installs them all and records them as `install_reason: "managed"` in the state file. This makes them hidden + locked.

For loose packs, dependencies are resolved from the repository:
```
hcli plugin install go-analysis-pack
```

Dependencies not found in the archive are fetched from the repository and recorded as `install_reason: "dependency"`.

### The distinction is emergent

- If all deps are in the archive: tight group behavior (atomic, hidden, locked).
- If deps must be fetched: loose pack behavior (independent, visible, manageable).

The same manifest field serves both cases. The behavioral difference comes from the packaging, not the schema.

### Pros
- Simplest schema change: one field, `dependencies`, array of strings.
- The tight-group behavior is a natural consequence of multi-plugin archives (which already exist).
- No new concepts to explain to plugin authors.
- Hex-Rays just packages everything in one archive. Community authors just list names.

### Cons
- The behavior depends on the *packaging context* (was the dep in the archive or not?), not on an explicit declaration. This can be confusing if a plugin is installed from one source (archive) but later upgraded from another (repository).
- No way for a manifest to *require* that deps be co-packaged. A community member could accidentally create a "tight group" by shipping a multi-plugin zip when they meant to create a loose pack.
- Harder to lint/validate: you can't tell from the manifest alone whether a plugin is meant to be a tight group or a loose pack.

---

## Proposal 5: `dependencies` with explicit version pinning for suites

For Hex-Rays paid extensions specifically, use the manifest to pin exact versions of all dependencies. The version pin is the signal that this is a tight group.

### Schema

Tight group:
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "hexrays-advanced-analysis",
    "version": "2.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "init.py",
    "dependencies": [
      { "name": "hexrays-taint-engine", "version": "==2.0.0" },
      { "name": "hexrays-type-propagation", "version": "==2.0.0" },
      { "name": "hexrays-call-graph-viz", "version": "==2.0.0" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Loose pack (no version pins):
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "go-analysis-pack",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "noop.py",
    "dependencies": [
      { "name": "go-runtime-detector" },
      { "name": "go-string-extractor" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Behavior

Pinned dependencies:
- HCLI ensures the exact version is installed. If the dep is co-packaged in the archive, extract from there. Otherwise, fetch the exact version from the repository.
- Upgrading the parent re-pins all deps to the new parent's declared versions.
- Users can't independently upgrade pinned deps (the parent's pin wins).

Unpinned dependencies:
- Fetch latest compatible version from the repository.
- After install, independently manageable.

### Pros
- Version pins are a natural, well-understood mechanism.
- One field, gradual spectrum from loose to tight via pinning.
- A suite that pins `==2.0.0` for all deps effectively moves as a unit on upgrade.
- Compatible with potential future version range syntax if needed.

### Cons
- Introduces version constraints between plugins, which the research strongly advises against. Every surveyed ecosystem that tried inter-plugin version constraints regretted it.
- Pinned versions require a resolver to check feasibility.
- Doesn't address hiding/visibility. A pinned dep is still a visible plugin.
- The "lock-step upgrade" is emergent from pins, not explicit. You'd need to also pin the dependency versions in the new version of the parent, and build/test them together. This is more fragile than co-packaging.

---

## My recommendation

**Proposal 1** is the strongest overall. It's closest to the apt/HA pattern that the research converges on, adapted for IDA's specific constraints. The `bundled: true` flag on individual dependencies is a clean, minimal distinction that maps directly onto your two requirements without creating separate resolver paths or introducing version constraints.

The key IDA-specific question it raises (subdirectory nesting for bundled components and whether IDA's plugin loader can handle it) is a constraint you'll hit with any proposal that tries to hide members from the user. That question deserves attention regardless of which proposal you pick.

Shall I dig deeper into any of these, or discuss the tradeoffs between specific proposals?

content.text:
Good feedback across the board. Let me address each point and then present a refined Proposal 1.

### 1. Distribution channels for tight packs

You're right, I over-indexed on co-packaging in a zip archive. Tight packs distributed through the private repo are the primary use case, not the edge case. The revised model: `bundled: true` means "must come from the same source and move together as a unit" regardless of the delivery mechanism (private repo, archive, local filesystem). When you `hcli plugin install hexrays-advanced-analysis` from the `hexrays` repo, HCLI resolves the parent, reads its dependencies, fetches each member from the same repo, and installs them together. The multi-plugin zip is one delivery option, not the defining characteristic.

This means we can't rely on co-packaging to "know" what belongs together. The manifest has to be explicit about it.

### 2. Individual component installation for development

Standalone installation of a member should work, especially for `hcli plugin install -e ./hexrays-taint-engine` during development. The collision rules:

- **Installing a suite when a standalone member already exists:** warn and offer to replace. The standalone version is superseded by the managed version. If editable, call this out specifically.
- **Installing a standalone member when a suite already manages it:** error with a clear message: *"hexrays-taint-engine is managed by hexrays-advanced-analysis; uninstall the suite first, or use --force to replace the managed copy."*
- **`hcli plugin status`** should distinguish a standalone install from a suite-managed one.

### 3. Explicit version pins for tight packs

Agreed. The parent's version should not implicitly govern members. Instead, the parent's manifest pins each member to an exact version:

```json
"dependencies": [
  { "name": "hexrays-taint-engine", "bundled": true, "version": "==2.1.0" },
  { "name": "hexrays-type-propagation", "bundled": true, "version": "==2.0.0" },
  { "name": "hexrays-call-graph-viz", "bundled": true, "version": "==1.5.0" }
]
```

When Hex-Rays releases suite v2.1.0, only the updated components get new version numbers. The suite's manifest updates the pins. Components that didn't change keep their existing versions. On upgrade, HCLI compares each member's installed version against the new pin and only re-fetches/re-installs the ones that differ.

For loose packs, version pins are optional. No pin = fetch whatever the repo has. This keeps the loose case simple.

### 4. Install-reason tracking: tradeoffs

This deserves a longer look. Let me lay out both sides.

**What install-reason tracking gives us:**

For tight packs (bundled): We need *some* way to know that `hexrays-taint-engine` is managed by `hexrays-advanced-analysis`. Without it, `hcli plugin status` can't tell whether the plugin was installed standalone or as part of a suite, and `hcli plugin uninstall hexrays-taint-engine` can't warn that it's managed. There are three places to store this:

1. **Central state file** (`$IDAUSR/plugins/.install-state.json`): One file, all relationships. Easy to query. Risk: file gets corrupted or out of sync.
2. **Per-plugin marker** (`.hcli-managed-by` file or annotation in the installed `ida-plugin.json`): Distributed, survives partial failures. But requires reading every plugin dir to reconstruct the graph.
3. **Subdirectory nesting** (`$IDAUSR/plugins/<suite>/<member>/`): The filesystem IS the state. But IDA's plugin loader only scans one level deep, so this requires either IDA-side changes or the suite's entry point to manually load members.

For loose packs: the question is really about whether `autoremove` is worth having. Without tracking:
- User installs `go-analysis-pack`, which pulls in 4 plugins.
- User uninstalls `go-analysis-pack`.
- The 4 plugins stay. User must manually uninstall each one.
- No way to distinguish "I explicitly installed go-string-extractor" from "it was pulled in by a pack."

**Can we avoid it for loose packs?**

At IDA's scale (users have 5-20 plugins, not 500), manual cleanup is feasible. When uninstalling a loose pack, HCLI could list the plugins that were declared as dependencies and suggest removing them, without needing to track install reason:

```
$ hcli plugin uninstall go-analysis-pack
Uninstalled go-analysis-pack.
These plugins were listed as dependencies and may no longer be needed:
  go-string-extractor  1.2.0
  go-type-recovery     0.9.1
  go-runtime-detector  2.0.0
Run `hcli plugin uninstall <name>` to remove them individually.
```

HCLI can produce this list by reading the manifest of the plugin *being uninstalled* right before removing it. No persistent state needed. It's less automatic than `autoremove` but simpler and avoids the state-synchronization problem. You lose the ability to distinguish "was this installed by the user or by a pack?" after the fact, but at this scale that might be acceptable.

**For tight packs, we can't avoid tracking entirely.** Members install to their own top-level directories (avoiding the IDA loader problem), so we need something to record the managed relationship. But it can be minimal: a `.hcli-suite` file in each member's plugin directory containing the suite name. This is distributed (per-plugin, not central), survives partial failures, and doesn't require a new central state file. HCLI reads it when it needs to check management status.

```
$IDAUSR/plugins/hexrays-taint-engine/.hcli-suite
# contains: hexrays-advanced-analysis
```

This gives us managed-member detection for tight packs without a central state file, and we skip install-reason tracking for loose packs entirely (relying on the uninstall-time manifest read for cleanup suggestions).

**The tradeoff summary:**

| | Central state file | Per-plugin marker | No tracking (loose) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tight pack management | Full support | Full support | Not possible |
| Loose pack autoremove | Full support | Reconstructible | Not supported; suggest instead |
| State corruption risk | Single point of failure | Distributed | N/A |
| Extra files to maintain | 1 central file | 1 file per managed member | 0 |
| Complexity | Moderate | Low | Lowest |

My recommendation: per-plugin marker for tight packs, no persistent tracking for loose packs (just read the manifest at uninstall time for suggestions). This avoids a central state file while covering the high-priority requirement.

---

## Refined Proposal 1

### Schema

A single `dependencies` field in `plugin`, containing objects with `name`, optional `bundled`, and optional `version`:

```json
{
  "IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion": 1,
  "plugin": {
    "name": "hexrays-advanced-analysis",
    "version": "2.1.0",
    "entryPoint": "init.py",
    "description": "Hex-Rays Advanced Analysis Suite",
    "urls": { "repository": "https://plugins.hex-rays.com/hexrays/advanced-analysis/suite" },
    "authors": [{"name": "Hex-Rays", "email": "support@hex-rays.com"}],
    "idaVersions": ["9.3"],

    "dependencies": [
      { "name": "hexrays-taint-engine", "bundled": true, "version": "==2.1.0" },
      { "name": "hexrays-type-propagation", "bundled": true, "version": "==2.0.0" },
      { "name": "hexrays-call-graph-viz", "bundled": true, "version": "==1.5.0" }
    ]
  }
}
```

Loose pack:
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "go-analysis-pack",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "entryPoint": "noop.py",
    "urls": { "repository": "https://github.com/community/go-analysis-pack" },
    "authors": [{"name": "Community", "email": "community@example.com"}],

    "dependencies": [
      { "name": "go-runtime-detector" },
      { "name": "go-string-extractor" },
      { "name": "go-type-recovery" }
    ]
  }
}
```

### Dependency object schema

```
name:     string, required. Plugin name.
bundled:  boolean, optional, default false.
            true = tightly coupled. Moves with the parent.
            false/absent = loosely coupled. Independently manageable after install.
version:  string, optional. Version specifier (e.g. "==2.0.0").
            Required when bundled=true.
            Optional for bundled=false (no pin = fetch latest from repo).
```

### Validation rules

- When `bundled: true`, `version` must be present and must use `==` (exact pin). No ranges.
- When `bundled: false`, `version` is optional. If present, supports `==` only for v1 (ranges deferred).
- All dependencies must be resolvable from the same source as the parent plugin. If the parent is in the `hexrays` repo, all deps must also be in the `hexrays` repo.

### Installation behavior

**`hcli plugin install hexrays-advanced-analysis`** (tight pack from repo):
1. Resolve parent from repo. Read its manifest.
2. For each `bundled: true` dependency, fetch the pinned version from the same repo.
3. Install parent to `$IDAUSR/plugins/hexrays-advanced-analysis/`.
4. Install each member to `$IDAUSR/plugins/<member-name>/`.
5. Write `.hcli-suite` marker file in each member directory (contains parent name).
6. If a member already exists as a standalone install, warn and replace (or error without `--force`).

**`hcli plugin install go-analysis-pack`** (loose pack from repo):
1. Resolve parent from repo. Read its manifest.
2. For each dependency, fetch from the same repo (latest compatible, or pinned version if specified).
3. Install parent and each dependency as independent plugins.
4. No marker files. No tracking beyond what the parent's manifest says.
5. If a dependency is already installed, skip it (already satisfied).

**`hcli plugin install -e ./hexrays-taint-engine`** (standalone/dev install of a member):
1. Normal editable install. Works fine.
2. If a suite already manages this name, error with message.

### Upgrade behavior

**Tight pack upgrade:**
1. Fetch new version of parent from repo.
2. Compare each member's pinned version against what's installed.
3. Fetch and upgrade only the members whose versions changed.
4. All-or-nothing: if any member fetch fails, roll back. (Uses the existing trash-based rollback mechanism.)

**Loose pack upgrade:**
1. Upgrade the pack itself. That's it.
2. Individual dependencies upgrade independently via their own `hcli plugin upgrade` calls.
3. If the new pack version added a dependency, it's fetched on upgrade. If it dropped one, it stays installed (user can remove manually).

### Uninstall behavior

**Tight pack uninstall (`hcli plugin uninstall hexrays-advanced-analysis`):**
1. Remove parent.
2. Remove all members that have `.hcli-suite` pointing to this parent.
3. Atomic: use the existing trash mechanism.

**Tight pack member uninstall (`hcli plugin uninstall hexrays-taint-engine`):**
1. Detect `.hcli-suite` marker.
2. Error: *"hexrays-taint-engine is managed by hexrays-advanced-analysis. Uninstall the suite to remove it."*
3. `--force` overrides: removes the member, leaves the suite in a broken state. Suite activation will fail (dep check).

**Loose pack uninstall (`hcli plugin uninstall go-analysis-pack`):**
1. Remove the pack plugin.
2. Read the pack's manifest (before deletion) and list dependencies that may now be unused.
3. Print suggestion to user: *"These plugins were dependencies and may no longer be needed: ..."*
4. Dependencies stay installed. User removes manually if desired.

### Status display

```
$ hcli plugin status
hexrays-advanced-analysis     2.1.0
  hexrays-taint-engine        2.1.0   (managed)
  hexrays-type-propagation    2.0.0   (managed)
  hexrays-call-graph-viz      1.5.0   (managed)
go-analysis-pack              1.0.0
go-runtime-detector           2.0.0
go-string-extractor           1.2.0
go-type-recovery              0.9.1
my-standalone-plugin          3.0.0
```

Managed members are indented under their suite. Loose pack dependencies are shown as independent plugins (no special grouping). The `--json` output includes a `managed_by` field for suite members.

### What this doesn't include (v1 scope)

- **No `after_dependencies` (soft deps).** Deferred until a real use case appears.
- **No `recommends`.** Same.
- **No version ranges.** Only `==` pins. No resolver needed.
- **No `autoremove` command.** Loose pack uninstall suggests cleanup instead.
- **No recursive packs (pack of packs).** Technically works (a pack can depend on another pack), but not tested or documented in v1.
- **No activation guard.** IDA loads what it finds; HCLI doesn't block IDA from loading a plugin whose deps are missing. This could be added later.

### Implementation scope in HCLI codebase

1. **Schema**: Add `dependencies` field to `PluginMetadata` in `__init__.py`. New Pydantic model for dependency objects.
2. **Install**: Extend `_install_plugin_archive` and the install command to resolve and install dependencies. The `# TODO: install idaPluginDependencies` at line 770 is the insertion point.
3. **Uninstall**: Extend to check `.hcli-suite` markers and cascade for tight packs.
4. **Upgrade**: Extend to diff pinned versions for tight packs.
5. **Status**: Extend to show managed relationships.
6. **Lint**: Validate dependency declarations (bundled must have version pin, same-source check).
7. **JSON schema**: Regenerate to include new fields.

---

What are your thoughts on this refined version? I'm particularly interested in whether the `.hcli-suite` marker file approach works for you vs a central state file, and whether the "suggest cleanup on uninstall" approach for loose packs is sufficient.

content.text:
Great feedback. These simplifications make the design much cleaner. Let me address each.

### 1. Version in the dependency string

You're right, using the same syntax as the CLI and as `pythonDependencies` is better than a structured object. The existing `split_plugin_version_spec()` in the codebase already parses `name==version` strings. So dependencies become flat strings:

```json
"hexrays-taint-engine==2.1.0"
```

No source prefix (always resolved from the same source as the parent). No structured object.

This raises the question of where the `bundled` flag lives. Two options:

**Option A:** Two separate arrays:
```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "hexrays-advanced-analysis",
    "bundledDependencies": [
      "hexrays-taint-engine==2.1.0",
      "hexrays-type-propagation==2.0.0",
      "hexrays-call-graph-viz==1.5.0"
    ]
  }
}
```

```json
{
  "plugin": {
    "name": "go-analysis-pack",
    "dependencies": [
      "go-runtime-detector",
      "go-string-extractor",
      "go-type-recovery"
    ]
  }
}
```

Both could appear on the same plugin if needed (a suite that also loosely recommends community plugins). `bundledDependencies` requires `==` pins; `dependencies` pins are optional.

**Option B:** Single array with a prefix convention:
```json
"dependencies": [
  "bundled:hexrays-taint-engine==2.1.0",
  "go-string-extractor"
]
```

Option A is cleaner. Two fields with clearly different semantics, flat string arrays matching existing conventions. The VS Code concern about two fields was specifically about the confusing interaction between them on uninstall, which we avoid because the semantics are distinct and non-overlapping: bundled = atomic, deps = independent.

I'd go with Option A. The field names are self-documenting, the string format is consistent with `pythonDependencies` and the CLI, and validation is straightforward: `bundledDependencies` entries must contain `==`, `dependencies` entries may or may not.

### 2 & 4. No marker files needed: derive relationships from manifests

You're right, and this is a better design. The manifests are already on disk. HCLI already scans all installed plugins via `get_installed_plugin_records()`. Building a reverse-dependency index from that scan is straightforward:

```python
def build_managed_plugin_index(records: list[InstalledPluginRecord]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Map member plugin name -> suite plugin name for all bundled deps."""
    managed_by: dict[str, str] = {}
    for record in records:
        for dep in record.metadata.plugin.bundled_dependencies:
            dep_name, _ = split_plugin_version_spec(dep)
            managed_by[dep_name] = record.name
    return managed_by
```

When `hcli plugin uninstall hexrays-taint-engine` runs, HCLI scans installed manifests, finds that `hexrays-advanced-analysis` declares it as a bundled dependency, and refuses (or warns). When `hcli plugin status` runs, it builds this index to show managed members indented under their suite.

This eliminates `.hcli-suite` marker files entirely. No extra state. The manifest IS the state. The cost is a full scan of installed plugin manifests, but that's already happening for most operations, and the result can be cached within a single command invocation (it's already cached in `get_installed_plugin_records()`).

One edge case: if the suite is uninstalled but its members somehow remain (interrupted uninstall, manual filesystem manipulation). In that case, the orphaned members have no parent manifest pointing to them. They just look like standalone plugins. This is actually fine: the worst case is the user sees them in `status` as regular plugins and can uninstall them manually. No broken state.

### 3. Interactive prompts on uninstall

For the parent → children direction (clear value):
```
$ hcli plugin uninstall hexrays-advanced-analysis
hexrays-advanced-analysis manages these plugins:
  hexrays-taint-engine        2.1.0
  hexrays-type-propagation    2.0.0
  hexrays-call-graph-viz      1.5.0
Uninstall all? [Y/n]
```

Default yes, since uninstalling a suite without its components makes no sense.

For the child → parent direction (less clear):
```
$ hcli plugin uninstall hexrays-taint-engine
hexrays-taint-engine is managed by hexrays-advanced-analysis.
Uninstalling it will break the suite. Continue? [y/N]
```

Default no, since this is a destructive/unusual action. No prompt about siblings; that's too much noise.

For loose pack uninstall:
```
$ hcli plugin uninstall go-analysis-pack
Uninstalled go-analysis-pack.
These plugins were listed as dependencies:
  go-runtime-detector    2.0.0
  go-string-extractor    1.2.0
  go-type-recovery       0.9.1
Remove them too? [y/N]
```

IDA will find and load ida-plugin.json at every level of nesting. There is no short-circuit.

The scanning function enumerate_fs_recursive() (base/plugins.cpp:1557) recurses unconditionally into every subdirectory up to depth 10. The visitor (visit_file, line 1903) always returns 0, so nothing ever stops the traversal early. Finding an ida-plugin.json in a parent directory does not prevent IDA from descending into child directories and finding more manifests there.

So a layout like this works:

~/.idapro/plugins/
  mybundle/
    ida-plugin.json        ← discovered at depth 1
    myplugin.dylib
    component-a/
      ida-plugin.json      ← also discovered at depth 2
      component_a.dylib
    component-b/
      ida-plugin.json      ← also discovered at depth 3... wait, depth 2
      component_b.dylib

All three manifests get parsed and registered.

The one constraint is the name field. Each ida-plugin.json must declare a unique plugin.name. When two manifests share the same name, the second one found is silently skipped (line 1960-1963) with a debug-level message. The traversal order within a directory is filesystem-dependent (whatever qfindfirst/qfindnext yields), so you can't rely on a particular one winning. As long as each manifest in the bundle declares a distinct name, all of them will load.

Other things to note:

- The entryPoint in each ida-plugin.json is resolved relative to that manifest's directory (line 1635-1637), so each component can point to its own binary.
- At depth 0 (files directly in plugins/), IDA uses legacy discovery (raw DLL/script files without manifests). The ida-plugin.json mechanism only activates at depth >= 1. So your bundle root must be a subdirectory of plugins/, not plugins/ itself — which matches the layout you described.
- Max recursion depth is 10, more than enough for any reasonable bundle structure.

For the HCLI use case: unpacking a bundle zip into ~/.idapro/plugins/mybundle/ where mybundle/ contains both a top-level ida-plugin.json and sub-directories with their own manifests will work. IDA will register every plugin it finds, each as an independent plugin keyed by its name.
